## Key Concepts

Machine learning 

Ex. Predicting rents based on median income Where do rents exceed our expectation? 

y = f(x) + e 

rent = function unknown + everything else 

**scale of rigid -> to flexible**
   
**rigid**
-- linear 
-- lasso/ridge 
-- logistic (trying to predict a binary, a classification problem)
-- trees + random forest
-- boosting
-- neural networks
**flexible** 


How to do this in R: 

m1 <- lm(med_rent ~ med_inc, data = tracts)
summary (m1)

(intercept) of med_inc  -- will return: estimate, S.E., t-value, p-value 

higher t-value, higher the confidence (greater than 1.96)

Cross Validation (cv)

k-fold - splits up the data 

Risks of overfitting: 
- trying to explain the explainable, not the unexplainable part of the model 

How to pick features? 
multicollinearity -> mostly harmless.. but check your prediction
